card.author: kofi
card.why: your team's scheduler, and kofi waits on you

item.title: Split the scheduler into lease and dispatch
item.author: kofi
item.body: The scheduler both leased jobs and dispatched them, so a slow dispatch held every lease. Leasing moves to its own loop; dispatch reads from a bounded channel. No behaviour change intended.

ai.summary: Splits the scheduler in two. Lease owns the jobs table: it hands out time-limited leases with a fencing token, renews them on heartbeat and reclaims expired ones every 15 s. Dispatch asks Lease for work, runs it and reports back with the token, so a worker that lost its lease can't overwrite a newer result. The old scheduler stays behind SCHEDULER_V2=false for a release and reads the same table, so a rollback needs no migration. Most of the 1,240 lines move existing code; about 300 are new, mainly the renewal loop and its tests.
concerns: Both services run migrations on start, so two replicas starting together can race on the new lease_token column.

intent.goal: Splits the scheduler into Lease and Dispatch so a worker that lost its lease can never overwrite a newer result.

steps.title: Leases and the fencing token
steps.body: Lease owns the jobs table: the new types and store hand out time-limited leases with a token, and the scheduler's entry point starts its loop.
steps.check: A renewal after the lease expired is refused, not extended.
steps.note: Lease ships first and runs alone for a release: Dispatch only starts asking it for work once SCHEDULER_V2 is on, so the old scheduler and Lease never hand out the same job.

steps.title: Dispatch reads from a channel
steps.body: Dispatch asks Lease for work through a bounded channel and reports back with the token.
steps.check: A full channel slows leasing instead of dropping jobs.
